_note: THE SEED MANIFEST FOR THE VIKUNJA BOARD. This file is data; vikunja_sync.py is dumb.
Card granularity is the NUMBERED PLAN.md ROW, because that is the unit PLAN.md itself
calls 'a place you can stop' (Phase 15's build-order note). Art cards use asset_request.md's
own P-numbers. Three phases that closed whole and list no open rows (6, 7, 10) get one card
each; everything else is a row.
The 'key' is the identity used for idempotent matching, and it is also the title prefix.
Never renumber a key: the sync matches on it, so a changed key creates a duplicate card
rather than updating one. If PLAN.md renumbers a row (its own header says this has happened
twice), fix the title and leave the key.
Done is seeded with the closures PLAN.md named explicitly for 2026-08-27..09-01 (and the
since-deleted PROGRESS.md, which is where several of the Done descriptions came from),
NOT with the project's whole history. Git and PLAN.md 12 are the archive; a board is a board.
Test is deliberately empty. Nothing is awaiting verification as of 2026-09-01.

project.title: AOD_mobile
project.description: Age of Dragons — mobile RTS. Status layer for PLAN.md (architecture + reasoning) and asset_request.md (the art queue). PLAN.md stays the authority: where this board and PLAN.md disagree, PLAN.md wins and the board is the one to fix.

cards.title: Scenario and campaign data, and the loader
cards.description:
campaign.json + scenario.json typed into CampaignDef/ScenarioDef (src/data/, plain RefCounted like every other def), read by a Campaigns loader walking PLAN.md 3.3's ROOT LIST — editor-only dev override first, then user://content/scenarios/. NOT an autoload: PLAN.md 6.1's table is exactly four and only the front door reads this.

PLAN.md 15.1 + 11.7 (schema and traps).

TRAP: the PNGs already on disk are NOT imported resources and load() cannot open them — outside res:// there is no .import sidecar and no --import step that would make one. Image.load() + ImageTexture.create_from_image() is the route. Load a 1920x1080 background when its campaign is opened, never all of them behind the selection list.

TRAP: a pinned seed is not a pinned map. MatchConfig carries seed as provenance only; any MapGenerator change makes the same seed produce something else. Acceptable for these three scenarios and only these three.

cards.title: The objective vocabulary, in the sim
cards.description:
MatchConfig.Mode.SCENARIO + MatchConfig.objectives, an ObjectiveSystem immediately BEFORE WinConditionSystem in the tick order, per-player objective progress on player_state. Headless-testable end to end with no screen in existence.

NOT a blocker for a playable campaign — scenario 3 is LAST_MAN_STANDING and needs none of it. This is what unlocks scenarios 1 and 2 and may trail the screens.

PLAN.md 15.2 + 11.8 (the vocabulary, which 16.6 also writes).

subject in unit/building/age/area/named_unit — area and named_unit are 16.5 and 16.7's and must be REJECTED AT LOAD until both ends exist, never silently evaluated as zero. owner in self/enemy/ally/index, routed through Diplomacy with the team table passed as a REQUIRED argument. compare in >=/<=/==, INTEGER ONLY. output in win/lose/alert. Multiple win rows are ANDed.

SCENARIO MODE MUST SUPPRESS LAST-MAN-STANDING'S WIN AND KEEP ITS LOSS. Call the elimination half and skip the sides half; do not copy the function. Otherwise killing the passive AI's five villagers wins scenario 1 with two villagers and no house.

cards.title: The launch path — ScenarioDef to MatchConfig
cards.description:
Two players (human + one Passive AI), map_type = RIVER, seed pinned in scenario.json, starting_age = 1, and the scenario's own mode — LAST_MAN_STANDING with no objectives, or SCENARIO with them. One function, tested by asserting the config rather than by starting a match.

A scenario is a MatchConfig, not a second way to start a match: 1.6's precedent is exact. Nothing in the boot path, the net layer or SimWorld.setup() needs to learn what a campaign is.

PLAN.md 15.3.

cards.title: Campaign selection screen
cards.description:
Replaces Campaign.tscn's placeholder body — the last front-door destination that is a placeholder rather than a feature. Row per campaign: icon left, title top, description right, both growing rightwards; BACK at the bottom. The frame, the scene change and the way out all already exist — this is a body.

PLAN.md 15.4, spec in scenarios/README.md.

cards.title: Scenario screen
cards.description:
Campaign title at the top, a SCROLLING column of scenario rows on the left with everything past `progress` locked, the campaign background plus title/description/PLAY in the main panel. Selecting a row swaps the main panel, it does not change scene.

A VBoxContainer overflows — it does not clip, scroll or compress past its children's minimum sizes. The lobby shipped with its bottom nav strip off the screen for exactly this reason and every structural test passed.

PLAN.md 15.5. Scenario 3 is playable at 15.1 + 15.3 + this.

cards.title: The scenario message and the objective tracker
cards.description:
A modal carrying scenario.json's `message`, dismissed by an X; and a small live panel listing each objective with its progress ('Villagers 4 / 10') read off player_state.

The message field is SHARED WITH SKIRMISH by the owner's spec, so it belongs to the match HUD and not to the campaign screens.

PLAN.md 15.6. If the tracker gets any control that is not a BaseButton, run preview_touch_controls — a Slider is inert under a thumb inside a match.

cards.title: Completion and unlock
cards.description:
On match_over with the local player winning, raise user://campaign_progress.json's counter for that campaign. ONE-WAY, A MAXIMUM, NEVER DECREMENTED — the same property that makes SimPlayer.defeated safe to read anywhere — and idempotent, because a result screen can be reached twice.

Progress is a separate file from the campaign folder because they have separate lifetimes: an update may replace a campaign's folder wholesale and must not take the player's place in it with them.

PLAN.md 15.7.

cards.title: The three How To Play scenarios (content only)
cards.description:
Three scenario.json files and one campaign.json against the icons already staged in scenarios/HowToPlay/. The row that is ONLY data if 15.1-15.7 did their jobs.

1 How To Gather and Build — SCENARIO — own >= 1 building.house AND >= 10 unit.villager
2 How To Age Up — SCENARIO — own age >= 2 (Age of Embers)
3 How To Find Opponent and Attack — LAST_MAN_STANDING — leave the enemy nothing

All three on a generated River map against a Passive opponent.

PLAN.md 15.8. Scenario 3 was settled as LAST_MAN_STANDING by the owner 2026-09-01: '0 enemy units' is unreachable against a Passive AI, which never stops training villagers.

cards.title: preview_campaign.tscn + tests
cards.description:
The preview photographs selection -> scenario -> launch. The TESTS are the load-bearing half, and there are FOUR cases rather than three:

1. Drive the sim to objective 1 and assert it fires.
2. Drive the sim to objective 2 and assert it fires.
3. Assert that wiping the opponent in SCENARIO mode does NOT win (decision 5, and the one no screenshot can see).
4. Drive scenario 3's conquest to a real LAST_MAN_STANDING result.

A win condition that never fires is invisible from every screenshot.

PLAN.md 15.9.

cards.title: Map save format
cards.description:
PROMOTED: it stopped being optional the moment a tool exists to write it. Phase 16's whole output is a map file and this is where that file's format is decided — building the tool first means inventing a second format and then reconciling two.

PLAN.md 11.3 carries the three rules the format must satisfy, and the promotion note.

TRAP: JSON.stringify encodes a PackedByteArray as a STRING ('[1, 2, 250]'), verified on 4.7.1. MapData.from_dict() already reads bytes, JSON's string, or a plain list. Everything else there was defended with int() because JSON numbers come back as floats; terrain was the one field that looked like it needed no conversion.

SAVING A MAP IS NOT SAVING A MATCH. What can come back is the map the match was STARTED with, which is GameScene's held map source. Round-tripping a half-built settlement with rubble in it is 12.4.

cards.title: MapMaker project skeleton
cards.description:
MapMaker/project.godot on the pinned 4.7.1, windowed desktop, plus the local config naming the game root and the startup hash check.

Deliverable is deliberately tiny: it launches, reads the game's data/*.json, and prints how many unit, building, resource and terrain entries it found. If that number is wrong, nothing built on top of it can be right.

THE COPIES CHECK THEMSELVES. MapMaker carries its own copy of map_data.gd, iso.gd and atlas_entry.gd (all three pure RefCounted maths). It reads the three originals AS TEXT from the configured game root at startup, hashes them, and REFUSES TO SAVE — loudly, naming the file — if they no longer match. A green tool that writes a stale format is worse than one that will not start.

A junction or symlink into game/ is REJECTED: this repo sits inside Google Drive sync and a link there is one more way to corrupt a .git that has been corrupted once already.

PLAN.md 16.1, spec in MapMaker/README.md.

cards.title: Vertical slice: iso canvas, terrain paint, save, and LOAD IN THE GAME
cards.description:
Grid overlay, paint each SimMap.Terrain, write 2.4c's format into repo-root maps/, then open it from the skirmish screen's map-source picker and PLAY it.

THIS IS THE ROW THAT PROVES THE CONTRACT, and it is worth doing before a single object can be placed. It also exercises PLAN.md 3.3's dev override in the direction that matters — the tool writes a folder the game reads without either of them going through res://.

PLAN.md 16.2. Depends on 2.4c.

cards.title: MapMaker object palette
cards.description:
Player 1-8 + Gaia dropdown, colour picker, category dropdown (Unit / Building / Area / Terrain), search filter, icons cropped from the staged atlases the way ControlGroupSlot already does it.

NEVER take unit_ids()/building_ids() order into the list — Array[StringName].sort() orders by StringName IDENTITY, not text, and identity order is not stable between runs. Sort explicitly.

PLAN.md 16.3.

cards.title: MapMaker placement and the three cursors
cards.description:
Select / move / edit, click to place, DRAG TO PLACE WALLS the way the game does. The wall art's facing is settled and measured (PLAN.md 12A's third wall finding) — mirror WallPlan's axis rule rather than re-deriving it.

Footprint collision uses the SIM's footprint, not the visual's measured extent. The two are different rects and both are right: the sim's is the tiles a building holds, the visual's footprint_m is the ground its mesh covers. An age-4 town centre overhangs its 8x8.

PLAN.md 16.4.

cards.title: MapMaker areas — named regions
cards.description:
A NEW MapData FIELD and therefore a FORMAT_VERSION BUMP, plus a matching reader on the game side.

Areas are what unlocks subject: 'area' in PLAN.md 11.8's objective vocabulary, and until both ends exist the loader rejects it.

PLAN.md 16.5.

cards.title: MapMaker Map Conditions editor
cards.description:
Writes PLAN.md 11.8's vocabulary and INVENTS NOTHING: the same subject/owner/compare/value/output records a hand-written scenario.json emits. Two dialects would let the tool author maps the game misreads.

It validates that there is at least one WIN and DOES NOT ASK FOR A LOSE — the README's 'at least one lose condition' requirement is dropped, because owning nothing is defeat on every map in this game whatever it declares. A map whose answer is 'beat them' therefore needs no conditions at all.

A time limit is one more row with subject: 'ticks' — and it must be TICKS, not seconds, for ages.json's reason.

PLAN.md 16.6. Depends on 15.2.

cards.title: MapMaker per-entity overrides and named units
cards.description:
THE EXPENSIVE ROW, and the only one with real sim cost. Health, attack, speed and a NAME on an individual placed entity means SimUnit/SimBuilding carry overrides, MapGen.build_from() applies them, and state_hash() MUST FOLD THEM IN or two clients disagree about how much hp a scripted hero has.

Named units are also what subject: 'named_unit' needs.

DO NOT START HERE. 16.2-16.6 are usable without it.

PLAN.md 16.7.

cards.title: MapMaker scenario export
cards.description:
Write a campaign.json / scenario.json pair and the icon slots beside the map, so a campaign is authored in the tool rather than by hand-editing JSON.

This is where 15.1's schema gets its SECOND CONSUMER, and the schema is the one that must not move.

PLAN.md 16.8. Depends on 15.1.

cards.title: MapMaker/HOW-To.md
cards.description:
The owner's ask, and it is written LAST on purpose: a guide to an interface still being built is a guide that will be wrong.

PLAN.md 16.9.

cards.title: Content: re-author the three How To Play maps, then The Dragon Born
cards.description:
Re-author the three How To Play maps for a custom look and feel, which also swaps their pinned SEEDS for pinned FILES and retires PLAN.md 11.7's seed trap. Then 'The Dragon Born', the second campaign, built entirely in the tool.

PLAN.md 16.10. Depends on 16.2 and 16.8.

cards.title: AssetPacks — manifest, download, verify, mount, and a download screen
cards.description:
The last open Phase 0 item, and it was PROMOTED from 'still open' to 'on the path' on 2026-09-01: a campaign cannot reach a phone until this exists, because authored content lives outside res:// and has to be installed into user://content/.

PLAN.md 3.2 (asset delivery) and 3.3 (content delivery).

cards.title: Building upgrades — a cost and a time for a non-gate upgrade
cards.description:
HALF-BUILT ALREADY: BuildingDef.upgrades_to, UpgradeBuildingCommand and SimWorld.convert_building all exist and have shipped a real upgrade since 5.8 — the wall-to-gate conversion, which mutates in place and keeps the entity id rather than respawning.

What is missing is what an upgrade that is NOT a gate needs: a COST (the gate inherits the wall's) and a TIME (it is instantaneous). The queue 9.3 taught to hold a research is the obvious place for the time.

The third question is ANSWERED: an upgrade is the per-building mechanism and a technology is the player-wide one. They stay two things.

PLAN.md 5.3, 15 item 1.

cards.title: The AI has no rule that researches
cards.description:
techs: true has been declared in every ai_profile since 12.2b against nothing, and 9.3 did not change that — it made it MATTER. ResearchCommand exists and no rule emits one.

Same shape as the hole 4.11's population counter was in: a field read by something that nothing writes. It is now a BALANCE hole too — a human who buys Blast Furnace is fighting an army that never will.

WARNING: the AI ladder's tick table in BUGS.md was measured before this and is not invalidated by it (neither side researches), but THE FIRST RULE THAT RESEARCHES INVALIDATES EVERY ROW.

PLAN.md 15 item 2.

cards.title: Camera-follow
cards.description: One of the two open Phase 3 rows. PLAN.md 3.5.

cards.title: Tap minimap to move
cards.description:
PLAN.md 3.7.

CHECK HIT-TEST ORDER FIRST. A Control laid over the minimap swallows every tap: the four corner buttons were a PRESET_FULL_RECT grid added OVER it and Godot hit-tested them first, so minimap click-to-move and double-tap-to-centre were both dead while looking implemented.

cards.title: Chat — the transport
cards.description:
Wireframe only; there is no transport behind it. ChatBoard exists and its tab row is 150 px PER PLAYER, which is one of the three width bugs the lobby's 50/50 split surfaced — the tabs scroll sideways now.

PLAN.md 8.6.

cards.title: Reconnect
cards.description:
LAN discovery landed 2026-08-31, so typing an IP is optional and this is the remaining hole in the same area: a dropped client cannot come back.

A rejoining client picks up stock, population, age, control groups and objective progress for free, because all of them travel on player_state.

PLAN.md 12.1b.

cards.title: Save/load and replays
cards.description:
Saving a MATCH, which is not saving a MAP (that is 2.4c). Round-tripping a half-built settlement with rubble in it is this row.

PLAN.md 12.4.

TRAP: JSON.stringify encodes a PackedByteArray as a STRING, and JSON numbers come back as floats. This and 2.4c are the two places sim data goes through JSON.

cards.title: Regicide — declared and inert
cards.description:
Conquest works; Regicide and Trophy are declared and inert. INERT IS THE SAFE DIRECTION TO BE UNFINISHED IN — _trophy()'s note is the precedent: 'you lose when your trophy dies' on a map with no trophies defeats everybody immediately.

PLAN.md 11.2.

cards.title: Trophy win condition — declared and inert
cards.description:
See 11.2. Declared, inert, and safe that way.

PLAN.md 11.

cards.title: The AI cannot see what it is fighting
cards.description:
A DECLARED CEILING, NOT A DEFECT. Opened 2026-08-27 with 12.2b: no rule in data/ai_*.json can see the opponent, so an army is a target number and never a response.

It is a REBUILD of 12.2b's condition vocabulary, not a bug fix, and it wants a game whose balance is settled first.

Note that PLAN.md 11.8's objective vocabulary DOES get the axis the AI lacks — owner: self/enemy/ally — because a win condition runs on the server and can see the whole world.

PLAN.md 14.

cards.title: Lobby wants faction and game-type controls it has no systems for
cards.description:
UI_Design_Lobby.png is ahead of the systems: it shows faction and team columns, a game type (Conquest / Regicide) and a victory-condition picker, a map-size choice and in-lobby chat.

Teams LANDED 2026-08-31. One civilisation is a locked v1 decision (PLAN.md 1) and Regicide is declared inert (11.2), so two of the four have no system to drive them.

PLAN.md 1.

cards.title: The two lobby setup panels do not both fit at 1152x648
cards.description:
The column scrolls. Flagged to the owner rather than guessed at.

A VBoxContainer overflows — it does not clip, scroll or compress past its children's minimum sizes — so any column whose child count the player controls needs a ScrollContainer round it. At eight player slots the GAME SETUP panel alone is taller than a 648 px viewport, and the first render had the map panel and the entire bottom nav strip off the screen with nothing to indicate they existed. Every structural test passed.

Related: shrinking something INSIDE the overflowing column does not move the fold — the fold is wherever the preceding sibling ends.

PLAN.md phase 1. (Originally recorded in PROGRESS.md's phase-1 row, deleted 2026-09-01.)

cards.title: The River map splits an allied pair across banks
cards.description:
THE RING OF STARTS IS ALREADY TEAM-SHAPED AND NOTHING WAS DONE TO IT: _start_positions spreads players evenly by index, so teams 1,1,2,2 land at 0/90 against 180/270 — allies adjacent, enemies opposite, for free.

THE RIVER IS THE EXCEPTION AND IS NOT FIXED: _river_start_positions alternates banks by i % 2 and so splits a pair. Fixing it means threading teams through MapGenerator.generate for one map type; flagged rather than done on 2026-08-31.

The archipelago separates allies by design (one island each) and that is a question for the owner, not a bug.

NOTE: Phase 15's three scenarios all run on generated RIVER maps, so this row is in the same file 15.3 will be pinning a seed against.

AGENT_GAME_CODER.md 7 (Teams).

cards.title: No way to clear a rally point
cards.description:
Rally points landed 2026-08-27: select one of your own buildings, tap bare ground, and a flag goes down; anything leaving that building walks to it — an ejected garrison AND every unit it trains. No waypoint means the old behaviour, unchanged.

MOVING one works. CLEARING one does not exist.

BUGS.md.

cards.title: Teams have no shared vision, and it is a measurement not a line
cards.description:
DELIBERATELY SKIPPED, not missed. It is one line in VisionSystem — and _reveal is 32 of 55 ms on an 8-player map, the hottest loop in the sim, and team vision roughly DOUBLES the tiles each player lights.

MEASURE test_tick_cost EITHER SIDE BEFORE LANDING IT. And note that test_tick_cost is the one thing in the suite that can fail for reasons that are not the code: it reported 49.81 ms on a loaded workstation and passed comfortably on the same commit forty minutes later. Re-run it alone before believing it.

Also absent by the owner's ruling and NOT to be read as gaps: shared unit control, repairing an ally's building, garrisoning in an ally's tower, and an AI that knows what an ally is. Owner 2026-08-31: 'we will not be interacting with any other player units or buildings, no garrison, no repair, no healing... happy with AI attacking opposing teams but not team members.'

AGENT_GAME_CODER.md 7 (Teams).

cards.title: More buildings — 23 buildings, ~70 bakes
cards.description:
BLOCKED ON ART A.10, not on code. Its own PLAN.md line has said 'low code effort, ~70 bakes behind it' since it was written, so it is paced by the art side's building roster and by nothing here.

PLAN.md 5.7.

cards.title: Civilisations
cards.description:
Art-paced. Note that ONE CIVILISATION IS A LOCKED v1 DECISION (PLAN.md 1), so this row is post-v1 by construction.

PLAN.md 9.5.

cards.title: The age re-skin
cards.description:
BLOCKED ON ART A.10. Every age skin this phase needs comes out of the building roster the art side is baking age by age.

The mechanism is already built and dense by contract: atlas_for(visual_id, age, colour) composes two independent axes, the ages map names all four ages explicitly, and _validate_skins() fails the suite on a gap. Two ages that look alike simply point at the same file. Buildings carry the age; units do not.

PLAN.md 9.6, 2.7.1.

cards.title: Dragons — the whole phase
cards.description:
BLOCKED ON ART, NOT ON SEQUENCING. vis.dragon carries exactly one clip — static, 1 frame, fps 1, loop false, across 8 stored directions — so the unit cannot walk, attack or die. speed: 0 is that, not a balance number.

NOTHING IS BLOCKED TODAY: the unit is real and trainable at the castle from age 4, and 4.10 gave it its fire breath over a 5x5.

See the P7 card: the art side has answered and it needs an owner decision, not more asset-agent time.

PLAN.md 13, asset_request.md [P7].

cards.title: ART — the building roster, age by age
cards.description:
DONE — the owner's call, 2026-09-01: "all assets excluding dragon, packed engines (trebuchet, onager) looks good, bugs may be reported but for now its considered complete."

The roster had in fact been delivered for some time and the card had not moved: every building the game declares carries a staged atlas, and visuals.json wires the four-age map for each. It was baked age by age as planned — age 1 five buildings, age 2 eight more, age-3 buildings two skins each, ages 1 and 2 deliberately NOT collapsed.

The assets the owner excluded are NOT recorded here, by their instruction of 2026-09-01: half-done work gets its own To-Do card rather than a note on a closed one. The dragon is P7, the packed siege pair is P6 and P9-packed-siege. None of the three is a building.

NOT closed by the check the board contract asks for — no colour/facing/clip pass was run over the building set. It is closed on the owner having played it. A bug found later reopens it rather than contradicting this.

Fields were the one loose end and are settled: they do NOT age. The game picks one of four at placement time and a field attaches to the mill; vis.field_1..4 map onto field_age2/3/4 and farm. tools/recipes/field_age2.toml carries the reasoning, including why those three must never be given a variant_seed.

asset_request.md delivered log, PLAN.md 12A A.10.

cards.title: ART — vis.dragon has no rig, and rigging it is real modelling work
cards.description:
ANSWERED BY THE ART SIDE 2026-08-30: IT CANNOT BE DONE CHEAPLY. This needs an owner decision, not more asset-agent time.

The premise in the request was wrong in a way that HELPS: the dragon is NOT bespoke art, it is 0 A.D.'s own, sitting at art/actors/fauna/dragon.xml. PLAN.md 12A A.9 has scheduled it as 'bespoke' since 0.9 on an assumption nobody checked.

The mesh genuinely has no rig, verified against PRISTINE art rather than a bake-damaged stub — art/meshes/skeletal/dragon.dae hashes to e7aa71ac95c6cda5..., which IS the sha256 in HEAD's git-lfs pointer. It contains one unrigged node, 454 triangles: library_controllers 0, library_animations 0, skin 0, joints 0, JOINT 0. And nothing to borrow from — no dragon in art/skeletons/ (78 definitions), no *dragon* under art/animation/, and neither actor group carries an <animations> block.

WHAT THE CORRECTION CHANGES, and it is the part worth the owner's attention: bespoke art would have meant commissioning. Upstream 0 A.D. art means the mesh is CC-BY-SA 3.0 — it can be rigged and the rig redistributed, on an attribution row LICENCES.md already has the shape for. At 454 triangles this is a small low-poly creature, not a film asset. So the job is 'someone rigs one small mesh we already own and are licensed to modify': bounded and quotable. The licence is not the obstacle and the modelling is not open-ended.

OWNER DECISION NEEDED: commission the rig, or leave the dragon a statue and phase 13 closed.

asset_request.md [P7].

cards.title: Answer the art side: is the dragon's footprint the wingspan or the ground?
cards.description:
OWED BY THE GAME SIDE. The art side re-measured as asked and no bake was needed: dragon.toml records 18.380 x 16.212 x 7.523 raw units -> 9.19 x 8.11 x 3.76 m. So visuals.json's [6.53, 6.53] / 2.69 is wrong on every axis and height_m should be 3.76.

THE FOOTPRINT IS A JUDGEMENT, NOT A MEASUREMENT, because 9.19 x 8.11 is the bounding box WITH THE WINGS SPREAD — the sprite's extent, not the ground the creature stands on. The art side asked which we want: 'If the footprint drives the selection ring, the wingspan is probably what you want; if it ever drives collision or pathing, it is far too big.'

GameView._ring_ground_m is where the split is already written down: a building's square traces the SIM's rect, a unit's ellipse is drawn from the VISUAL's. So the answer is probably the wingspan — but confirm what else reads footprint_m before saying so, and note that height_m 3.76 can be corrected today either way.

asset_request.md [P7], AGENT_GAME_CODER.md 6 ('a footprint and a measured extent are two different rects').

cards.title: ART — confirm footprint_m for five animals and five carcasses
cards.description:
Ten isobake inspect runs: vis.wolf, vis.bear, vis.boar, vis.fish, vis.deer_carcass and the five newer carcasses. NOTHING IS BLOCKED and nothing looks wrong — these are shipped as estimates and only the art side can measure them.

WHY THE GAME SIDE COULD NOT: height_m derives exactly from the anchor and reproduces vis.tree, vis.sheep and vis.cattle to the last digit. footprint_m DOES NOT COME OUT OF THE ATLAS — animals are authored non-square (the sheep is [1.5, 0.65]) so one frame cannot give both axes, and calibrating the crop against three known animals gives 23.3 / 23.6 / 31.3 px/m along the length against 21.4 / 21.5 / 15.4 across, which is not a constant.

AND THE INVERSION FAILS OUTRIGHT ON A BODY LYING DOWN — negative height for four of the five new carcasses (the wolf's E frame gives -0.35 m). Structural, not a choice of frame.

THEY NOW NEED A RE-BAKE FIRST: art_work/out was emptied 2026-08-30 (9.46 GB). isobake inspect reads the SOURCE actor and still works, so the ten measurements are still one inspect each — but anything wanting to re-read a baked frame costs a bake. Taking P5 and P6 together in one sitting is the cheap ordering.

WHAT THEY AFFECT, AND IT IS NOT GAMEPLAY: the selection-ring size and Occlusion.column_pad_for's outline band.

WORTH ONE LOOK: a straight frame crop makes the bear's carcass and the wolf's the same size (both 58 px on E), which cannot be right for a 150 hp bear and a 30 hp wolf.

RE-DERIVE ANYTHING TAKEN OFF THE OLD DEER SPRITES — the deer carcass was re-baked 2026-08-28.

asset_request.md [P5].

cards.title: ART — player colour for the two colourable packed siege actors
cards.description:
vis.onager_packed and vis.trebuchet_packed each need 8 colour atlases. Their DEPLOYED halves carry 8 each; the packed twins carry none, so a blue player's onager turns plain the instant it packs and blue again when it sets down.

NOT BLOCKING — 4.13 shipped without it and this is the visible seam it left. Cosmetic, and only while a siege engine is moving.

vis.ballista_packed IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THAT LIST: the lithobolos art set measures 0% playercolour and its deployed form has no colour bake either, so the packed one matching it is correct rather than missing. That is one actor's measurement and not a rule about siege — re-measure rather than assume, in BOTH directions (vis.ballista measures 0.00% and the ram 6.8%).

All three ids are in visuals.json with `colours` ABSENT (not false by oversight), so adding the bakes is a one-word change on the game side.

16 sequential bakes: colour variants bake at -Parallel 1.

WORTH KNOWING: vis.ballista and vis.onager's declared `placeholder` figures no longer reproduce from their own current atlases — derived before the 2026-08-27 yaw re-bake and out by ~0.1 m and ~0.3 m. Harmless (a placeholder only draws when the pack is missing) and recorded so it does not read as a bug.

See also P9-packed-siege: the owner reported these two engines as not looking good, which is a WIDER complaint than colour.

asset_request.md [P6].

cards.title: ART — the packed trebuchet and onager do not look right
cards.description:
RAISED BY THE OWNER 2026-09-01, closing A.10: 'all assets excluding dragon, packed engines (trebuchet, onager) looks good.' Filed as its own card rather than as a note on the closed A.10, per the owner's instruction the same day.

WHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN IS WHICH DEFECT THEY SAW. Two are already on record and they need different work, so ask before baking:

1. vis.trebuchet_packed HAS NO CREW AT ALL. The four Han engineers hang off the pivot actor, and this recipe deliberately bakes the wagon one level down instead — the owner's own call of 2026-08-28, taking a clean animated ox-cart over four frozen and mostly headless soldiers. Reversing it means fixing the prop_anchor_count tie-break that AGENT_ASSET.md 4 says is defeated by identical crew, AND the Blender COLLADA importer refusing the mangonel_infantry_* clips. Not small, and it was traded away knowingly.

2. NEITHER CARRIES PLAYER COLOUR, so both go plain the instant they pack and colour again when they set down. That is P6 and it is 16 sequential bakes.

If it is something else — a pose, a scale, a facing — say which and it is measurable: art_work/out is empty, so re-reading a baked frame costs one 12-second directions=1 probe first.

vis.ballista_packed is NOT in this card: its deployed half measures 0% playercolour, so the packed one matching it is correct.

asset_request.md [P6], tools/recipes/trebuchet_packed.toml.

cards.title: ART — 27 technology icons
cards.description:
DONE — and it was done on 2026-08-30, by card P8, which this card should have been closed alongside. THESE TWO CARDS ARE THE SAME WORK: P8 says so in its own text, 'filed as 27 tech icons and widened the same day to the entire UI'. Widening the scope left the narrow card behind in Blocked, still saying the icons were backlogged and every research tile drew its name.

VERIFIED ON DISK 2026-09-01, not taken from P8's word: all 27 tech.* ids in game/data/techs.json have a 100x100 PNG in game/assets/ui/icons/ and an entry in selection_actions.gd's ICONS map, with tech_generic.png as the declared fallback for a 28th tech added later. The art is Docs/ART_PROMPT.md's sheet_d_military_techs (blacksmith 12 + university 2 + fallback) and sheet_e_economy_techs (13, two cells reserved), generated by the owner and sliced into assets/UI_Gen/sliced/icons.

Owner, 2026-09-01: 'we generated and added it to the game, it looks good.'

THE LESSON IS THE DUPLICATE, NOT THE ICONS. A card that is a subset of another card does not close itself when the superset ships, and nothing on the board points one at the other. Both cards now cross-reference.

asset_request.md Delivered 2026-08-30, Docs/ART_PROMPT.md.

cards.title: Decide: teach isobake to exempt the root bone from location_scale
cards.description:
THE ART SIDE OFFERED AND IS WAITING FOR A WORD. location_scale = 0.0 is the correct fix for the deer's per-direction distortion and it also zeroes the ROOT bone's location curve — which is the one carrying a dying body's drop to the ground. So THE DEER CARCASS NOW FLOATS about 5 px (~0.22 m): its lowest pixel sits 4-8 px ABOVE the anchor where the wolf's sits 17-35 px below.

Standing and walking are unaffected. It will bias an anchor-derived height by roughly that much, which matters to P5's measurements and to nothing else.

The art side: 'Fixing it properly means teaching isobake to exempt the root bone from location_scale — say the word and I will; it did not seem worth holding the deer fix behind.'

DECISION: take the isobake change, or accept a 5 px float and let P5 measure around it.

asset_request.md [P5], art-side note of 2026-08-28.

cards.title: Special abilities — monk heal, dragon fire breath
cards.description:
CLOSED 2026-08-29 with the rest of Phase 4, on the owner's instruction to close out the open steps. Both were promised in IDEA.md long before they existed. The dragon breathes fire over a 5x5 for 40 damage.

AbilitySystem._is_hostile_to is one of the two owner clauses that did not go through Diplomacy and was missed on the first Teams pass.

cards.title: Stances — four, military defaults Defensive
cards.description:
CLOSED 2026-08-29. A soldier now defends itself and walks back to where it was standing; a villager does not. It was a decision CombatSystem's header had written down twice.

STANDING HAZARD IT LEFT: a fixture that puts two hostile units near each other and expects nothing to happen was safe for the whole life of the project and stopped being safe that day. Six tests broke and not one was about stances. The fix is to say what the fixture means (u.stance = SimUnit.Stance.PASSIVE), never to reach for the default.

Also: unit.militia declares los: 4 against StanceSystem.GUARD_RADIUS's 5, so reading def.los straight made AGGRESSIVE see LESS than DEFENSIVE on six of the roster's units. _sight_of floors it. When one setting is meant to be strictly stronger than another, assert the ORDERING, not the numbers.

cards.title: Siege pack/unpack state machine
cards.description:
CLOSED 2026-08-28 with SiegeSystem. All three engines travel packed and fight deployed, automatically, on an order rather than on a button.

It waited on art since 2026-08-22 for a real reason: every siege atlas staged was the unpacked pose, so the machine had no way to show its two states apart and building it against a magenta placeholder would have proved the transition happened without proving it was the right way round.

The one thing left is cosmetic and is the P6 card.

cards.title: Formations — line, grid, vee, box
cards.description: CLOSED 2026-08-29. The four the selection panel had offered as greyed placeholders since 4.3 — which is why it was cheap: the menu had named its four shapes for months.

cards.title: The tech tree — 27 technologies at seven buildings
cards.description:
BUILT 2026-08-29 on the owner's instruction, AHEAD OF PHASE 5. Bought from an action tile on the building that holds them.

PLAN's promised TechSystem turned into TechMods, a static modifier resolver, because a research rides the building's existing PRODUCTION QUEUE — so the timer, the progress bar, the cancel and the refund were all already there.

TWO THINGS IT LEFT BEHIND rather than closed: the AI still researches nothing (its own card), and 5.3's open question is now answered — an upgrade is the per-building mechanism and a technology is the player-wide one.

TRAP IT TAUGHT: a percentage modifier on a base rate of 1 is a modifier of ZERO. TechMods.scaled(1, 25) is 1. An 'Architecture, +25% build speed' tech was written, costed, and removed the same hour because BuildSystem.BUILD_RATE is 1 progress per builder per tick. Ask what the BASE is before choosing between a flat bonus and a percentage.

cards.title: The tech-tree page
cards.description:
BUILT 2026-08-29 behind the minimap. The read-only guide to what is where, and it ISSUES NO COMMAND AT ALL — the owner's own ruling, and what that page has claimed about itself since it was written.

The icons are backlog: every tile draws its name.

cards.title: The [X] clear-selection button
cards.description:
BUILT 2026-08-28. The only thing on PLAN.md 15's list the owner reported from actually playing a build, and it turned out to be a LAYOUT problem rather than a UI one: the HUD's left edge had exactly 40 px of unspent height between the control-group stack and the selection panel's ceiling, so the button's size was decided by arithmetic rather than chosen.

The gesture and right-click both stay.

cards.title: Archipelago, and the transports that had to ship with it
cards.description:
CLOSED 2026-08-29. One island per player, a few sheep, nothing hostile — PREDATORS is keyed by map type and read with .get(type, {}), so an unlisted type gets no predators without a line of code.

TWO THINGS IT COST: MapValidator required every start to reach every other BY LAND, which an archipelago fails by definition, so that claim had to CHANGE rather than relax. And transports had no load/unload, so an archipelago was a map on which NO PLAYER COULD REACH ANOTHER and no win condition could fire — both shipped together rather than the type going out as a sandbox.

RETUNED 2026-08-30 on the owner's playtest: islands grown from radius 18 to 26, with the BOARD now derived from the island (128 / 160 / 240 at 2 / 4 / 8 players) rather than the island capped by the board.

STILL MISSING: naval combat. A loaded transport crosses unopposed. And the archipelago separates ALLIES by design — a question for the owner, not a bug.

cards.title: Settings — as an overlay rather than a screen
cards.description:
CLOSED 2026-08-30.

ITS VOLUME SLIDERS WERE INERT UNDER A THUMB INSIDE A MATCH from the day they landed and every test was green. emulate_mouse_from_touch is off for exactly as long as a match lasts, and Godot's Slider reads mouse events only. A BaseButton answers a raw touch; nothing else in this project does. They are TouchSliders as of 2026-08-30, and preview_touch_controls exists because nothing in the repo exercised a finger.

cards.title: HOW TO PLAY
cards.description:
CLOSED 2026-08-30. Six annotated captures of this game's own HUD, one to a page, behind the front-door button that had answered with a 'not available yet' toast since 1.1.

Every front-door button now opens a screen except QUIT — and Campaign.tscn is the last one whose body is a placeholder, which is 15.4.

cards.title: The AI rule engine — five real difficulties
cards.description:
DONE 2026-08-27. It grew from 're-tune it' into a rule engine: five difficulties driven by resource triggers in data/ai_*.json instead of a script of timed steps.

The owner's summary of why it matters: 'the update system support customization and supports random maps, thats the big win from this update.'

IT OPENED PHASE 14 as a declared ceiling: no rule can see the opponent. And it declared techs: true against nothing, which is still open.

cards.title: LAN discovery and the server browser
cards.description:
LANDED 2026-08-31. A UDP beacon on Net.PORT + 1 and a live server browser behind the lobby's SERVERS button, so typing an IP is now optional. The wireframe went live the same day it was built.

TWO TRAPS IT TAUGHT: JSON.parse_string() pushes an engine error PER FAILURE where JSON.new().parse() does not — irrelevant on a config file and a hole on a socket, since LanBeacon.decode reads whatever the network sends it. And a disabled control's REASON for being disabled is not the same fact as its being disabled: JOIN came out enabled with nothing to join, because an empty list needs no explanatory sentence.

The rest of UI_Design_Hosting.png implies a master server, which LanBeacon's header argues against by name.

cards.title: Teams — four hostility predicates widened together
cards.description:
LANDED 2026-08-31. SimPlayer.team was declared at 0.4 and read by NOTHING for the life of the project. Now: a one-character -/1/2/3/4 picker per lobby slot, MatchConfig.teams on the wire, and four predicates widened at once — Diplomacy.is_enemy, .is_enemy_fact, CombatSystem._is_at_war_with, AISystem._nearest_enemy.

THREE PROPERTIES WORTH KEEPING:
- The team argument is REQUIRED with no default. A default would have shipped the old behaviour in the one place nobody looked; GDScript reports a missing argument at parse time.
- 0 IS THE ABSENCE OF A TEAM, not a team everybody shares. 'Equal teams are allies' would make the entire back catalogue of fixtures one enormous alliance.
- A TEAM GAME WITHOUT A TEAM WIN CONDITION IS A HANG. WinConditionSystem counts SIDES: two teammates standing is two standing players and nothing can reduce it to one.

The minimap tints allies sky blue #87CEEB, chosen by MEASUREMENT — sky blue and water are six degrees apart in hue, so hue is not what separates them; CIE L* is, at 79 against shallow water's 51.

Two owner clauses did not go through Diplomacy and BOTH were missed first time: StanceSystem._may_start_on and AbilitySystem._is_hostile_to keep their own owner check for BUILDINGS. An aggressive soldier would have shot an ally's barracks while doing exactly the right thing about their soldiers.

cards.title: ART — the whole UI art set, every panel button and icon, replaced once
cards.description:
DELIVERED AND WIRED 2026-08-30, 9b0ae14..60f8184. Filed as 27 tech icons and widened the same day to the entire UI because the owner settled the question it was asking: 'we will be replacing all art including Kibyra's.'

14 Gemini prompts, generated by the owner, sliced into 130 pieces with 0 flagged — 103 icons and 22 chrome pieces, which prepare_ui_chrome.py renders out as the 29 that ship.

THE WIN WAS LICENCE, NOT LOOKS: Kibyra's terms forbade redistribution, which is why game/assets/ui/ was gitignored and a clean checkout had no HUD. licence_audit.py went 129 problems -> PASS and a fresh clone now runs with its chrome intact. Fonts are Cinzel Decorative + New Rocker, both OFL 1.1, each shipping beside its own licence text.

THREE HANDOVER FIGURES DID NOT SURVIVE CONTACT and the measurement beat the table: panel_hud 46 not 64; panel_ornate 183/241/178/92 not 256; and measure_ninepatch.py finds a STRETCHABLE RUN, which is not a nine-patch margin — a margin has to clear the corner, and the dragon's neck reaches 70 px past the bead band.

A NinePatchRect's border is drawn at 1:1 and SHRINKING THE MARGIN MAKES IT WORSE. The only lever is the SOURCE SIZE.

P8-TECH-ICONS IS THE SAME WORK AS THIS CARD and was left in Blocked when this one closed. Both were verified on disk and closed 2026-09-01.

asset_request.md Delivered, 2026-08-30.

cards.title: Phase 6 — resources and wildlife
cards.description:
CLOSED 2026-08-23, whole. No open rows.

Wildlife animations and six carcasses delivered 2026-08-28. THE LESSON THAT OUTLIVED IT: a clip only one species has, sent by the sim for all of them. Only the deer has run and only the cattle has feeding, and the generic fallback chain static -> idle would have five of six animals STANDING STILL WHILE SLIDING at flee speed. AtlasEntry._ANIM_ALIAS (run -> walk, feeding -> idle) is tried ahead of that chain, and the test for whether an alias belongs there is that it falls back to a clip every subject HAS.

cards.title: Phase 7 — the resource HUD
cards.description:
Closed, whole. No open rows.

Cross-cutting 7.5 audio is BUILT (2026-08-23) — AudioManager, MatchAudio, data/audio_map.json, 131 sound ids. What is left there is BYTES: the 0 A.D. fetch is rate-limited and incremental, and a clean checkout runs silently by design.
